rows.selection_reason: With no completed experiments, there is zero evidence about any design axis (modality, encoder, profile strategy, aggregation, fusion). The most informative first step is to establish a minimal, well-understood baseline. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) uses the simplest standard RNA representation (PCA, 2000 components), avoids confounding from multi-profile aggregation or fusion choices, and is computationally lightweight. It anchors the RNA performance floor against which every subsequent experiment—image-only, multimodal, alternative encoders, multiprofile—can be compared. Establishing this floor first lets the next experiments directly test whether adding images, switching encoders, or using multimodal fusion provides a meaningful gain, making each follow-up experiment maximally interpretable under the limited budget.

1) Evidence/uncertainty: We have only one completed experiment (config_001: RNA-only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 → 48.5% acc). We have zero information about whether the image modality carries any discriminative signal. This is the most fundamental uncertainty in a multimodal study. 2) What this tests: config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) isolates the image modality's contribution under the same singleprofile setting, giving us a clean second unimodal baseline to compare against the RNA-only result. 3) Why it's the best next experiment: Before investing in multimodal fusion configurations (which change modality, add an image encoder, and introduce a fusion strategy simultaneously), we must know whether the image features are informative at all. If image-only performs comparably to RNA-only, multimodal fusion becomes highly promising and we can prioritize those configs next. If image-only is much weaker, we should focus on RNA encoder/aggregation improvements. This single experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the most important design axis (modality contribution) and directly guides the next 2-3 experiments in the budget.

Evidence: config_001 (RNA-only, PCA, singleprofile) achieves 0.485 accuracy, establishing RNA as the dominant modality, while config_010 (image-only, ResNet50) is very weak at 0.208, suggesting image contributes little signal on its own. This makes the RNA representation quality the most critical design decision for any future multimodal experiment. Question tested: Does a learned nonlinear RNA encoder (scvi_n200) outperform the simple linear PCA (pca_n2000) baseline? This is a clean single-variable change from config_001, isolating the encoder choice. Why this is the best next experiment: The RNA encoder underpins every downstream multimodal configuration (configs 016–051). If scvi_n200 substantially improves on 0.485, it justifies investing in learned encoders for multimodal fusion; if it does not, PCA is sufficient and we should focus budget on profile/aggregation/fusion choices instead. This experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the most impactful design axis before committing budget to more complex multimodal or multiprofile configurations.

Evidence: RNA-only models (0.485–0.520) substantially outperform image-only (0.208), and scvi_n200 > pca_n2000 for RNA encoding. The critical unresolved question is whether multimodal fusion adds value at all, given how weak the image modality is in isolation. Config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat) is a clean ablation against config_001 (same RNA encoder, same profile setting) with the only change being the addition of resnet50 image features via concat fusion. This directly tests whether the image modality contributes complementary signal or introduces noise. Resolving this early is the highest-value use of the next experiment: if multimodal does not improve over RNA-only, an entire branch (~36 configs) can be deprioritized, freeing budget for RNA-only multiprofile and scgpt experiments. If it does help, we gain a validated direction to exploit with better encoders and fusion strategies.

Evidence: scvi_n200 clearly outperforms pca_n2000 in the RNA-only setting (0.520 vs 0.485, ~3.5% gap), and the current best result is multimodal with pca_n2000+resnet50+concat (0.527), which barely exceeds scvi RNA-only. Uncertainty: it is unknown whether the RNA encoder advantage carries into the multimodal setting, and whether the modest image contribution from resnet50 is sufficient to justify the added complexity. This experiment (config_028: multimodal, singleprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, concat) is a clean single-variable comparison to config_016, isolating the RNA encoder effect in the multimodal context. If it substantially beats 0.527, it confirms scvi_n200 is the right backbone for further multimodal exploration; if it plateaus near 0.520, it signals that resnet50 adds little and we should pivot to a stronger image encoder (ViT-L) or multiprofile strategies. Under a tight budget, this is the highest-information next step because it directly extends the strongest observed signal (better RNA encoder) into the most promising model family (multimodal) while keeping all other variables fixed for a clean attribution.

Evidence: All 5 completed experiments used singleprofile. The best config (config_028: scvi_n200 + resnet50 + concat) achieves 0.536 acc / 0.516 F1, confirming scvi_n200 as the superior RNA encoder and that multimodal fusion with resnet50 adds value. However, the multiprofile axis (with aggregation over multiple cellular profiles) is entirely unexplored, representing a major source of uncertainty about whether richer cellular representations can push performance further. Question: config_030 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + avgpool + concat, multiprofile) is the minimal, direct extension of config_028—same encoders, same fusion—changing only the profile representation from single to multiple with average-pool aggregation. This cleanly isolates the effect of multiprofile aggregation. Why this is the best next experiment: It tests the single largest unexplored design axis while holding all other variables at their best-known settings. If multiprofile+avgpool improves on 0.536, it opens a productive direction (then test transformer aggregation, ViT-L, weighted fusion). If it does not, we gain strong evidence that singleprofile suffices, saving budget from exploring 20+ multiprofile variants. Under a limited budget, resolving this binary question is more informative than, e.g., testing weighted fusion (a smaller expected delta) or a new image encoder (a secondary axis given image-only performance was very weak at 0.208).

Evidence: The largest performance jump in the study came from switching singleprofile→multiprofile (config_028: 0.536 → config_030: 0.632, +10 pts), with avgpool aggregation. scvi_n200 consistently outperforms pca_n2000, and concat fusion is the only fusion tested in the multiprofile regime. Uncertainty: We have only tested one aggregation method (avgpool) for multiprofile. It is unclear whether a transformer-based aggregation could capture richer inter-profile interactions and push performance further, or whether avgpool is already near-optimal. What this tests: config_032 is a clean one-variable change from the current best (config_030), replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping scvi_n200, resnet50, and concat fusion fixed. This isolates the effect of the aggregation mechanism. Why this is the best next experiment: The aggregation method is the dimension most directly responsible for the largest observed gain, so resolving whether transformer aggregation helps (or hurts) relative to avgpool is the highest-information single experiment. It either opens a promising new direction (if transformer >> avgpool) or confirms avgpool sufficiency, allowing budget to be redirected to other axes (e.g., fusion method or image encoder).

Evidence: config_032 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) is the best so far at 0.688 acc / 0.659 F1, confirming that multiprofile + transformer aggregation + scvi_n200 + concat fusion is a strong recipe. However, the image encoder remains at resnet50, which performed very poorly as image-only (0.208 acc), suggesting the image modality may be underutilized. Question: Does upgrading the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (a substantially larger, ImageNet-pretrained ViT) meaningfully improve multimodal performance while keeping all other winning settings fixed? Why this is the best next experiment: It is the single highest-impact untested axis in the context of our top configuration. The image encoder is a major design lever with only one option (resnet50) explored in the multiprofile multimodal regime, and the weak image-only baseline hints that a stronger encoder could unlock additional signal. Testing config_038 isolates the image-encoder effect cleanly, reducing uncertainty about whether to invest further in image quality or pivot to other axes (fusion type, scgpt RNA encoder).

Evidence: The best configuration so far (config_038, acc=0.721) uses multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion. All top-performing experiments use concat fusion; weighted fusion has never been tested in the multiprofile+transformer+ViT-L regime. Question: Does weighted fusion outperform concat when all other components are at their best-known settings? This isolates fusion strategy as the single variable changed from the current best. Why this is the best next experiment: It is a minimal, targeted extension of the strongest configuration, directly testing an important and unexplored design axis (fusion method) without introducing multiple confounding changes. The result will either yield a new best configuration or confirm that concat is optimal, reducing uncertainty about a key architectural choice with a single experiment.

Evidence: The current best (config_039, 0.7250) uses scVI as the RNA encoder with ViT-L, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion in a multiprofile multimodal setup. We have strong evidence that learned RNA representations (scVI) outperform linear ones (PCA) by ~1-4 points across settings, but scGPT—a generative model-based encoder—has never been tested in any multimodal configuration. This is the largest remaining source of uncertainty about the RNA encoder choice. Question: Does scGPT match or exceed scVI in the optimal multimodal pipeline? Why this experiment: config_051 (scgpt, ViT-L, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) is a single-variable swap from the current best (config_039), isolating the RNA encoder effect. A positive result would identify a new promising direction; a negative result would confirm scVI as the best RNA encoder and redirect budget toward other levers (e.g., fusion refinements or additional image encoders). Under a limited budget, resolving this high-impact uncertainty with a clean A/B comparison is the most efficient use of the next experiment.
